citations.desc: Attending veterinarian and adequate veterinary care (dealers and exhibitors).
citations.narrative:
There are several bottles of expired medications intermingled with non-expired medications intended for administration to
animals as needed: Ivermectin injection (expiration date illegible), Vitamin B Complex (expired 09/2025), Epinephrine
injectable (expired 10/2025), and Fenbendazole Oral Liquid (expired 01/2026). Utilizing expired medications or items with
unknown expiration dates compromises animal welfare. Expired drugs may suffer from reduced potency or altered
chemical composition, rendering them ineffective or capable of inducing adverse side effects. Failing to maintain facility
pharmaceuticals can leave animal illnesses untreated or cause unnecessary distress from unrelieved symptoms.
Furthermore, using expired emergency drugs like Epinephrine means critical life-saving interventions or anesthetic
reversals may fail when urgently required. The licensee must use appropriate methods to prevent, control, diagnose, and
treat diseases and injuries. Out-of-date medications are not appropriate methods to comply with this requirement.
TO BE CORRECTED FROM THE DATE OF THIS INSPECTION ON 09/25/2026 AND GOING FORWARD.
This inspection and exit interview were conducted with the facility representative.
You may appeal all or part of any inspection report by submitting a written statement contesting the findings—along with
any supporting documentation—to the Deputy Administrator. Appeals of routine, focused, or attempted inspections must
be received within 21 days of report issuance as shown by the signature line of this report.
Appeals may be sent by email to AnimalCare@usda.gov.
Appeals sent by mail should be addressed to:
Deputy Administrator
APHIS Animal Care (AC)
U.S. Department of Agriculture
2150 Centre Avenue, Building B
Mailstop #3W11
Fort Collins, CO 80526-8117
